ITQAN:v2p415/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p415/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p415/r16.claim: Dhikr can refer to ritual prayer.

JISHUMI:v5p3579/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r5.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r5.claim: Al-Aṣamm says prayer reminds people of their sins, leading them to repent and avoid evil, as in the statement that prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r5.anchor: كقوله: (إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر)

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p358/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p358/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p358/r11.claim: Prayer is the familiar ritual prayer, which restrains from indecency when performed with its obligations, sunnahs, humility, reflection, and awareness of standing before God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p358/r11.anchor: والمعنى: من شأنها أنها إذا أديت على ما يجب من فروضها وسننها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p358/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p358/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي وابن جريج وحماد بن أبي سليمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p358/r12.claim: They say prayer restrains from evil while the worshipper is engaged in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p358/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والكلبي، وابن جريج، وحماد بن أبي سليمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r1.claim: A worshipper seen committing sins does not pray in the manner described, so the verse does not promise that every prayer always restrains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r1.anchor: وأما من تراه من المصلين يتعاطى المعاصي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r2.speaker: ابن بحر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r2.claim: Ibn Baḥr interprets الصلاة as supplication, meaning to direct supplication toward God's command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r2.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: الصلاة: الدعاء، أي أقم الدعاء إلى أمر الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r3.claim: A person's sinning does not disprove the verse: it says prayer has the characteristic of restraining, not that every prayer always does so; prayer must be of the described kind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r3.anchor: ولا يدل اللفظ على أن كل صلاة تنهى، بل المعنى، أنه يوجد ذلك فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r4.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r4.claim: A report says an Anṣārī youth who prayed with the Prophet nevertheless committed indecencies and theft; the Prophet said his prayer would restrain him, and the youth soon repented.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث أن فتى من الأنصار كان يصلي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r5.speaker: عبد الله وسلمان وأبو الدرداء وابن عباس وأبو قرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r5.claim: They interpret ولذكر الله أكبر as God's remembrance of people being greater than their remembrance of Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r5.anchor: فقال عبد الله، وسلمان، وأبو الدرداء، وابن عباس، وأبو قرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r6.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r6.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd understand God's remembrance as greater than everything.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة، وابن زيد: أكبر من كل شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r7.claim: Other views say remembrance in prayer earns greater reward than outside prayer, exceeds other pillars of prayer, or that God's remembrance is stronger than prayer's restraint and greater than all worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r7.anchor: وقيل: ولذكر الله في الصلاة أكبر منه خارج الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes remembrance as greater without qualification: mindful remembrance restrains inside or outside prayer, whereas bodily movements have no such effect and mere speech ranks lower.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وعندي أن المعنى: ولذكر الله أكبر على الإطلاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says prayer is greater than other acts of obedience, is itself called God's remembrance, and reminds people that God sees their deeds and will reward or punish them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p359/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يريد والصلاة أكبر من غيرها من الطاعات

RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r1.claim: If Muhammad grieves over their disbelief, reciting revelation consoles him: Noah, Lot, and other messengers delivered their message and proofs without rescuing their people from error; recitation here is for his comfort, not directed to them.
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r1.anchor: إن كنت تأسف على كفرهم فاتل ما أوحي إليك لتعلم أن نوحا ولوطا وغيرهما

RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r2.claim: Unlike a one-time message, a scripture containing universal law must be read repeatedly, preserved before people's eyes and in their hearts, transmitted across generations, and brought to mass transmission; the Qur'an is such a guide and healing for all people.
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r2.anchor: قسم يكون فيه قانون كلي تحتاج إليه الرعية في جميع الأوقات

RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r3.claim: Razi also classifies books as stories repeated only for others, technical works repeated only for oneself, and exhortations repeated for oneself and others because they renew delight, soften hearts, and displace distracting thoughts; the Qur'an belongs to the third class despite its stories and laws.
RAZI-FULL:v25p63#2/r3.anchor: كتاب لا تكره قراءته إلا للغير كالقصص

RAZI-FULL:v25p64/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p64/r1.claim: The commands to recite and pray console the Prophet: as messenger between God and people, when people do not accept his message he can turn toward God through prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64/r1.anchor: الرسول واسطة بين طرفين من الله إلى الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v25p64/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p64/r2.claim: Worship comprises belief, verbal remembrance, and bodily action. Belief already persisted in the Prophet and was established through direct vision beyond demonstration, so only repeatable recitation and bodily prayer are commanded.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64/r2.anchor: والعبادة البدنية كذلك فأمره بهما فقال : أتل الكتاب وأقم الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r1.claim: Some commentators take prayer to mean the Qur’an, which contains prohibitions against indecency and wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين المراد من الصلاة القرآن وهو ينهى أي فيه النهي عنهما

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi rejects the Qur’an reading because the preceding command to recite revelation makes this sense of prayer difficult to understand.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r2.anchor: لأن إرادة القرآن من الصلاة في هذا الموضع

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r3.claim: Some say prayer prevents wrongdoing only while the worshipper is performing it, since he cannot engage in either act then.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم أراد به نفس الصلاة وهي تنهى عنهما ما دام العبد في الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi rejects mere restraint during prayer as insufficient praise: many other activities, including sleep at its proper time, also prevent wrongdoing temporarily.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r4.anchor: ليس المراد هذا وإلا لا يكون مدحا كاملا للصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r5.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that prayer which does not restrain a person from sins only increases his distance from God; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r5.anchor: نقل عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi holds that a prayer valid under Islamic law restrains its worshipper from both sins in an unrestricted way.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r6.anchor: الصلاة الصحيحة شرعا تنهى عن الأمرين مطلقا

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r7.claim: A prayer intended for God and for showing off is legally invalid and must be repeated; al-Razi compares this with a disputed mixed intention in ablution.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r7.anchor: حتى لو قصد بها الرياء لا تصح صلاته شرعا وتجب عليه الإعادة

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r8.claim: Like a servant close to a great, generous king, a worshipper who serves God will not abandon that service to obey the expelled devil.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r8.anchor: أن يترك خدمة الملك ويدخل في طاعة ذلك المطرود

RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r9.claim: Prayer clothes the worshipper in piety as he stands before God; this spiritual attire makes indecent acts as unfit as filth is for someone wearing fine brocade.
RAZI-FULL:v25p64#2/r9.anchor: فكذلك العبد إذا صلى لبس لباس التقوى لأنه واقف بين يدي الله

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r1.claim: Because prayers recur, the piety they clothe the worshipper in and the resulting abstention from sins continue over time.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r1.anchor: إن الصلوات متكررة واحدة بعد واحدة فيدوم هذا اللبس فيدوم الامتناع

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r2.claim: Like an official who receives a fixed seat with a king, the worshipper enters God’s service and should not return to the station of sinners.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r2.anchor: إذا دخل في خدمة ملك وأعطاه منصبا له مقام خاص

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r3.claim: Al-Razi reads the office analogy as divine protection: whoever prays is guarded by God against indecency and wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r3.anchor: من صلى عصمه الله عن الفحشاء والمنكر

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r4.claim: Prostration brings nearness to God (96:19); repeated prayer raises the worshipper’s rank until even minor sins become repugnant to him, let alone major ones.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r4.anchor: فإذا زادت قربته وارتفعت منزلته حتى صار أميرا

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r5.claim: Another rational reading, confirmed by transmitted evidence, is that recitation and prayer forbid atheism and associating partners with God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r5.anchor: وفي الآية وجه آخر معقول يؤكده المنقول

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r6.claim: Al-Razi defines atheistic negation as denying God’s existence and associating partners as affirming divinity for someone besides God.

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r7.claim: Atheism is indecent because indecency is manifest ugliness, while God’s existence is clearer than the sun and every thing bears a sign of God.

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r8.claim: If calling a wife a mother is condemned as a manifestly wrong statement (58:2), then claiming that God has daughters is even more reprehensible because God cannot beget.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r8.anchor: فالمشرك الذي يقول الملائكة بنات الله

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r9.claim: Allahu akbar rejects atheism and association: Allah negates denial of God, while akbar excludes a partner equal in their shared attribute of greatness.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r9.anchor: لأن الشريك لا يكون أكبر من الشريك الآخر

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r10.claim: Bismillah negates atheism; al-Rahman and al-Rahim negate association by naming God as creator of existence and merciful giver of continued life through provision.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r10.anchor: إذا قال بسم الله نفى التعطيل

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r11.claim: Al-hamdu lillah counters denial of God, while Rabb al-alamin counters association by affirming God’s lordship over all worlds.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r11.anchor: أثبت بقوله الحمد لله خلاف التعطيل

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r12.claim: Fronting iyyaka in iyyaka naʿbudu rejects atheism and association; the same refutation applies to iyyaka nastaʿin.

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r13.claim: Seeking guidance to a path refutes atheism because it presupposes an aim; calling it straight refutes association because direct worship is nearer than worshipping idols as intercessors.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r13.anchor: المستقيم هو الأقرب والمشرك يعبد الأصنام

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r14.claim: The closing testimony that there is no god but God rejects both association and atheism.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r14.anchor: يقول فيها أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r15.claim: Prayer begins and ends with the name Allah, signaling that the worshipper remains with God from its first words to its last.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r15.anchor: أن الصلاة أولها لفظة الله وآخرها لفظة الله

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r16.claim: The worshipper should not imagine independence from the Prophet after reaching God; his exalted rank depends on Muhammad’s guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r16.anchor: أنت في هذه المنزلة الرفيعة بهداية محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r17.claim: Having recognized the Prophet’s guidance, the worshipper should remember his beneficence by blessing him.

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r18.claim: After returning from the prayer’s ascent to the community, the worshipper offers them peace, like travelers exchanging greetings.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r18.anchor: فسلم عليهم وبلغهم سلامي كما هو ترتيب المسافرين

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r19.claim: Prayer’s awe-filled form begins with standing before God like a slave before a king and ends with kneeling as one honored with a seat.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r19.anchor: وقوف بين يدي الله كوقوف المملوك بين يدي السلطان

RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r20.claim: One who kneels before God in this life will not kneel in the afterlife among the wrongdoers described in 19:72.
RAZI-FULL:v25p65/r20.anchor: لا يكون له جثو في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r1.claim: God’s remembrance is greater than remembrance of ancestors, whose good qualities people recall with full hearts and voices; it should receive the utmost reverence.
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r1.anchor: لكن ذكر الله أكبر ، فينبغي أن يكون على أبلغ وجوه التعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r2.claim: The omitted comparison does not name anyone whose remembrance God exceeds; al-Razi says this makes the phrase assert that greatness belongs to God alone, as in Allahu akbar.
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r2.anchor: مع حدف بيان ما هو أكبر منه لطيفة

RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r3.claim: Because God knows what people do and prayer is their best deed, they should perform it with reverence.
RAZI-FULL:v25p66/r3.anchor: وهذا أحسن صنعكم فينبغي أن يكون على وجه التعظيم

BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r1.claim: Tilawa means reading in sequence; wahy is communication in secrecy, and the divine word conveyed to prophets and saints is also called revelation.
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r1.anchor: التلاوة القراءة على سبيل التوالي والإيحاء إعلام في الخفاء ويقال للكلمة الإلهية التي تلقى إلى الأنبياء والأولياء وحي

BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r2.claim: Muhammad is to read the Quran to draw near God, preserve its wording, reflect on its meanings and realities, and remind people to practice its rulings, fine manners, and noble character; each thoughtful reading can disclose new insights.
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى : اقرأ يا محمد ما أنزل إليك من القرآن تقربا إلى الله بقراءته وتحفظا لنظمه وتذكرا لمعانيه وحقائقه

BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r3.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r3.claim: A thief who did not know the Quranic rule for theft asked Umar why his hand was being cut; after Umar recited 5:38, the thief said he would not have stolen had he heard it, but Umar did not excuse him.
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r3.anchor: فقال له عمر : بما أمر الله في كتابه

BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r4.claim: The source says congregational tarawih was established so people could hear the Quran.
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r4.anchor: فسن التراويح بالجماعة ليسمع الناس القرآن

BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r5.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r5.claim: Ali reports rewards per Quran letter: 100 good deeds standing in prayer, 50 seated in prayer, 25 outside prayer while in ablution, and 10 without ablution.
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r5.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه من قرأ القرآن وهو قائم في الصلاة كان له بكل حرف مائة حسنة

BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri says Quran reading outside prayer is better than a prayer containing little recitation; jurists likewise prefer long standing to many prostrations, citing the report that the best prayer has long standing.
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r6.anchor: وعن الحسن البصري رحمه الله : قراءة القرآن في غير الصلاة أفضل من صلاة لا يكون فيها كثير القراءة

BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r7.claim: The source recommends reciting in ablution, seated toward the qibla, without crossed legs or leaning, and in a humble posture like sitting before someone one respects.
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r7.anchor: قالوا : أفضل التلاوة على الوضوء والجلوس نحو القبلة وأن يكون غير مربع ولا متكىء

BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r8.claim: For further etiquette and spiritual secrets of recitation, the source refers readers to its discussion at the end of Surat al-Naml.
BURSEVI:v6p343#2/r8.anchor: وقد سبق في آخر سورة النمل بعض ما يتعلق بالتلاوة من الآداب والأسرار فارجع

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r1.claim: The prayer is the regular obligatory prayers performed in congregation; the Prophet's command to establish them also implicitly commands his community.
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r1.anchor: وحيث كانت الصلاة منتظمة للصلوات المكتوبة المؤداة بالجماعة وكان أمره عليه السلام بإقامتها متضمنا لأمر الأمة بها

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r2.claim: Prayer's characteristic effect is to prevent its performers from indecency and evil: fahsha is what reason deems vile, and munkar is an act forbidden by sacred law.
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r2.anchor: {تنهى} أي من شأنها وخاصيتها أن تنهاهم وتمنعهم

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r3.speaker: الوسيط
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r3.claim: Al-Wasit defines munkar as what is not acknowledged in any revealed law or sunna, whether word or deed; its opposite is ma'ruf.
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r3.anchor: قال في "الوسيط" : المنكر لا يعرف في شريعة ولا سنة أي سواء كان قولا أو فعلا والمعروف ضده

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r4.claim: An Ansari youth prayed the five daily prayers with the Prophet yet committed every kind of indecency; the Prophet said prayer would stop him, and the youth soon repented and became a devout Companion.
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r4.anchor: كما روي أن فتى من الأنصار كان يصلي مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلوات الخمس ثم لا يدع شيئا من الفواحش

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r5.claim: Every deed has a characteristic effect: prayer awakens fear of God and restrains sin, while unbelief, set against abandoning prayer in a hadith, stirs fear of people and attraction to forbidden acts (3:151).
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r5.anchor: لا شك أن لكل عمل خيرا أو شرا خاصية فخاصية الصلاة إثارة الخشية من الله والنهي عن المعاصي

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r6.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r6.claim: A hadith says that a person whose prayer does not keep him from indecency and evil only grows more distant from God; the source explains that such prayer becomes a liability.
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث "من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر لم يزدد من الله إلا بعدا"

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r7.claim: Some define prayer's reality as presence of heart through remembrance and watchful thought: remembrance expels heedlessness, while contemplation expels blameworthy thoughts.
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r7.anchor: كما قال بعضهم : حقيقة حضور القلب بنعت الذكر والمراقبة بنعت الفكر

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r8.claim: True prayer restrains sin both during and outside prayer, including the urge to admire one's deeds or demand recompense; it is the gnostic's delight because it rests on witnessing rather than absence.
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r8.anchor: فهذه الصلاة كما تنهى صاحبها وهو في الصلاة عما ذكر كذلك تنهاه وهو في خارجها عن رؤية الأعمال وطلب الأعواض

BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r9.claim: Obligatory or voluntary prayer is the best bodily act because it powerfully reforms the soul, the source of all indecency and evil.
BURSEVI:v6p343#3/r9.anchor: والصلاة فريضة كانت أو نافلة أفضل الأعمال البدنية لأن لها تأثيرا عظيما في إصلاح النفس

BURSEVI:v6p345/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345/r1.claim: One reading takes this to mean prayer surpasses other acts of obedience; it is called remembrance, as in 62:9, because remembrance of God is central to its superiority and power to restrain sin.
BURSEVI:v6p345/r1.anchor: {ولذكر الله أكبر} أي والصلاة أكبر من سائر الطاعات وإنما عبر عنها بالذكر كما في قوله تعالى : {فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله}

BURSEVI:v6p345/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345/r2.claim: Alternatively, remembrance of God is the greatest obedience: its reward is God's remembrance of the servant, as in 2:152 and the hadith qudsi about God's reciprocal remembrance.
BURSEVI:v6p345/r2.anchor: أو ولذكر الله أفضل الطاعات لأن ثواب الذكر هو الذكر كما قال تعالى : {فاذكرونى أذكركم}

BURSEVI:v6p345/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r3.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v6p345/r3.claim: The Prophet quotes God as saying He is with the servant who remembers Him, remembering the servant privately in response to private remembrance and in a greater assembly in response to public remembrance.
BURSEVI:v6p345/r3.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : "يقول الله تعالى : أنا عند ظن عبدي بي وأنا معه حين يذكرني

BURSEVI:v6p345/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345/r4.claim: Pure remembrance, clearer than remembrance mixed with outward deeds, surpasses fighting, freeing slaves, and giving wealth; it begins with tawhid, then detachment, then individuation, as the hadith about the mufarridun indicates.
BURSEVI:v6p345/r4.anchor: فالمراد بهذا الذكر هو الذكر الخالص وهو أصفى وأجلى من الذكر المشوب بالأعمال الظاهرة

BURSEVI:v6p345/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v6p345/r5.claim: The Prophet said the mufarridun have outstripped others; when asked who they were, he answered that they are men and women who remember God abundantly.

BURSEVI:v6p345/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345/r6.claim: Bursevi cites Sheikh al-Attar's poem saying detachment begins by bidding desire farewell and reaches complete severance from pleasure; freedom from hope in created things yields benefit from individuation.
BURSEVI:v6p345/r6.anchor:
أصل تجريد وداع شهوتست
بلكه كلى انقطاع لذتست

BURSEVI:v6p345/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345/r7.claim: Remembrance drives away heedlessness; some therefore say Paradise has no remembrance because it has no heedlessness, only the residents' constant presence.
BURSEVI:v6p345/r7.anchor: والذكر طرد الغفلة ولذا قالوا : ليس في الجنة ذكر أي لأنه لا غفلة فيها

BURSEVI:v6p345/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p345/r8.claim: Al-Tawilat al-Najmiyya reads indecency and evil as signs of heart-sickness, whose root is forgetting God; remembrance removes this illness more than recitation or prayer because its cure is the opposite of the disease.
BURSEVI:v6p345/r8.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : ما حاصله أن الفحشاء والمنكر من أمارات مرض القلب ومرضه نسيان الله

BURSEVI:v6p345/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345/r9.claim: Although recitation, prayer, and remembrance may issue from a forgetful heart, the divine response in 2:152 makes remembrance an elixir that overcomes the heart's illness; the servant's remembrance is absorbed into God's, making it greater.
BURSEVI:v6p345/r9.anchor: فأبطل خاصية المعلولية وجعله إبريزا خاصا بخاصيته المذكورة فذكر العبد فني في ذكر الله فلذا كان أكبر

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r1.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r1.claim: Some Sufi authorities say remembrance of the Essence in annihilation and the Real's prayer in established subsistence surpass all remembrances and prayers.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار : ذكر اللذات في مقام العناء المحض وصلاة الحق عند التمكين في مقام البقاء أكبر من جميع الأذكار

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says God's remembrance is greater than yours: His generosity is uncaused, whereas human remembrance is mixed with defects, wishes, and requests.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : ذكر الله أكبر من ذكركم لأن ذكره والكرم بلا علة

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r3.claim: Some object that comparing God's remembrance with the servant's compares the Eternal with the created; nothing matches God's eternity or remembrance, and the cosmos vanishes under the Creator's dominion.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إذا قلت : ذكر الله أكبر من ذكر العبد قابلت الحادث بالقديم

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r4.claim: Another says God's remembrance is greatest because it is obedience, while remembrance of anything else is not; woe to those whose time passes in remembering others.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : (ذكر خداي بزركتراست ازهمه جيزيراكه ذكر أو طاعتست

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r5.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r5.claim: Hafiz says time spent happily with the Friend is good time; all else is fruitless and heedless.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r5.anchor: قال الحافظ : أوقات خوش آن بودكه بادوست بسررفت باقى همه بيحاصل وبيخبرى بود

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r6.claim: God knows remembrance and the means of obedience, conceals nothing, and will reward them with the finest recompense.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r6.anchor: {والله يعلم ما تصنعون} من الذكر وسائط الطاعات لا يخفى عليه شيء فيجازيكم بها أحسن المجازة

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r7.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r7.claim: Some Sufi authorities say certainty that God knows every state and station leads one to avoid sins, turn to the Knower of secrets in worship, especially prayer, and empty the heart of distractions; one present prayer outweighs a thousand inattentive ones.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار : والله يعلم ما تصنعون في جميع المقامات والأحوال فمن تيقن أن الله يعلم ما يصنعه تجنب عن المعاصي

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r8.claim: A man who prayed with Habib al-Ajami disliked the outward recitation and restarted; in a dream he was told God had granted him an accepted prayer, whose value he failed to recognize.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r8.anchor: حكي : أن واحدا كان يتضرع إلى الله أن يوفقه لصلاة مقبولة فصلى مع حبيب العجمي

BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r9.claim: Repairing the inner state matters most: inner quality differentiates people and their rewards, and true success is escape from contingent existence through the generosity of the Necessary Being; Sharia and the Path open the way to true existence.
BURSEVI:v6p345#2/r9.anchor: فإصلاح الباطن أهم فإن به يتفاضل الناس وتتفاوت الحسنات ويحصل الفلاح الحقيقي

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r1.speaker: IJ, Q, R
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r1.claim: “Prayer” here refers to the obligatory prayers.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r1.anchor: Here prayer refers to the obligatory prayers (IJ, Q, R)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r2.speaker: IJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r2.claim: Some interpret “prayer” as Quran recitation, a form of supererogatory worship; al-Rāzī rejects this because the verse already commands Quran recitation.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r2.anchor: Some say it means the act of reciting the Quran (IJ, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r3.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī argues against interpreting prayer as recitation because the verse has already mentioned reciting the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r3.anchor: al-Rāzī argues against such an interpretation, given that the verse already begins with the mention of reciting the Quran

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r4.speaker: IJ
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r4.claim: The paired commands may mean that prayer prevents sin when one reflects on the Quran recited during it.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r4.anchor: The combined command to recite the Quran and perform the prayer can be understood to mean that if one performs the prayers and then reflects upon the words of the Quran recited in them

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r5.speaker: IJ
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r5.claim: Others understand prayer in and of itself to prevent indecency and abomination.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r5.anchor: though others understand this verse to mean that prayer in and of itself fulfills this function (IJ)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r6.speaker: Prophet / Ibn Masʿūd
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r6.claim: A saying, variously attributed to the Prophet or his Companion Ibn Masʿūd, says prayer that fails to prevent indecency and abomination only increases distance from God.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r6.anchor: According to a saying sometimes attributed to the Prophet and sometimes to his Companion Ibn Masʿūd

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r7.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r7.claim: Prayer may not prevent sin without sincerity and repentance; God accepts only from the reverent, as 5:27 says.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r7.anchor: prayer in and of itself may not prevent indecency and abomination unless it is combined with sincerity and repentance, as in 5:27

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r8.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r8.claim: The Prophet says a young man who prayed with him but inclined toward indecency would soon be restrained by his prayer.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r8.anchor: Surely his prayer will soon prevent him [from doing that]” (Bḍ, Q, Z)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r9.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r9.claim: Indecency may mean fornication, while abomination may mean disobedience.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r9.anchor: Here indecency may refer to fornication and abomination to disobedience (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r10.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r10.claim: The Prophet compares the five daily prayers to washing in a river five times daily: prayer removes one’s sins just as washing removes filth.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r10.anchor: the Prophet asked his Companions, “Tell me, if one of you had a river at his door in which he washed five times a day

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r11.speaker: al-Ghazzālī
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r11.claim: Al-Ghazzālī says prayer was prescribed to polish the heart and renew remembrance of God, not merely to perform its words and motions.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r11.anchor: al-Ghazzālī advises penetrating deeper into prayer, since it was not prescribed merely for the words and motions it entails

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r12.speaker: al-Tustarī
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r12.claim: Al-Tustarī says prayer that does not restrain shameful and unjust acts, and lacks the adornment of shunning them, is tainted and must be purified.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r12.anchor: al-Tustarī is reported to have said, “Every prayer that does not restrain shameful and unjust deeds

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r13.speaker: IJ, Sh, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r13.claim: One meaning is that remembering God is greater than everything else, including other acts of worship.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r13.anchor: The remembrance of God is surely greater (or “greatest”) means that to remember God is greater than all else (IJ, Sh, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r14.speaker: Bḍ, IJ, Sh, Su, Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r14.claim: Another meaning is that God’s remembrance of human beings exceeds their remembrance of Him.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r14.anchor: From another perspective, it means that God’s remembrance of human beings is greater than their remembrance of God (Bḍ, IJ, Sh, Su, Ṭ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r15.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r15.claim: This reading is explained by God’s remembrance being eternal while human remembrance is temporal.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r15.anchor: since His remembrance is eternal and theirs is temporal (Su)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r16.speaker: Sh, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r16.claim: Some hold that both the believer’s remembrance of God and God’s remembrance of believers are meant at once.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r16.anchor: or both meanings can obtain at the same time (Sh, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r17.claim: Sufi interpretation joins both senses: full remembrance requires annihilation of selfhood, so God remembers Himself through people beyond time and place.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r17.anchor: From a Sufi perspective, the two meanings together indicate that the fullness of remembrance comes only when individuals have been annihilated before God

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r18.speaker: IJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r18.claim: Some read the phrase to mean that remembering God during prayer is greater than the indecency and abomination prayer prevents.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r18.anchor: Some also understand this verse to mean that remembering God in prayer is better than the indecency and abomination that it prevents (IJ, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r19.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r19.claim: Another reading is that believers’ remembrance of God is greater than idolaters’ remembrance of their gods.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r19.anchor: that believers’remembrance of God is better than idolaters’ remembrance of their gods (R)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r20.speaker: Bḍ, Z
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r20.claim: A further reading takes “remembrance of God” as prayer, which is greater than every other act of obedience.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r20.anchor: what is meant by the remembrance of God in this verse, is better than all other acts of obedience (Bḍ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:29:45/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r21.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r21.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that the world and everything in it are accursed except remembrance of God and what supports it.
STUDYQURAN:29:45/r21.anchor: the Prophet is reported to have said, “The world is accursed, accursed is all that is in it

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the Prophet is to recite what was revealed to him, namely the Qurʾān.

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r2.claim: He explains the command as performing the prayer God prescribed, observing its bounds; he links the wording to Hūd 11:114.
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r2.anchor: يعني: وأد الصلاة التي فرضها الله عليك بحدودها

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmar interprets “prayer” here as the Qurʾān recited in mosques.
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر، " {إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: القرآن الذي يقرأ في المساجد "

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says prayer contains a restraint and deterrent from disobeying God.
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء، والمنكر} [العنكبوت: 45] يقول: في الصلاة منتهى ومزدجر عن معاصي الله "

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r5.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Abbas warns that prayer which does not restrain a person from evil only increases his distance from God.
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قول الله " {إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء} [العنكبوت: 45] والمنكر من لم تنهه صلاته

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r6.claim: When told a man prayed often, Ibn Masʿūd replied that prayer benefits only someone who obeys it.
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r6.anchor: عن سمرة بن عطية، قال: قيل لابن مسعود: إن فلانا كثير الصلاة، قال: « فإنها لا تنفع إلا من أطاعها»

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says prayer that does not command right and forbid wrong only increases distance from God.
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r7.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد، عن ابن مسعود، قال: «من لم تأمره صلاته بالمعروف، وتنهه عن المنكر، لم يزدد بها من الله إلا بعدا»

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd attributes to the Prophet the statement that there is no prayer for one who does not obey prayer, whose obedience is restraining evil.
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن مسعود، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «لا صلاة لمن لم يطع الصلاة، وطاعة الصلاة أن تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر»

TAB-FULL:v18p408/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r9.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r9.claim: Sufyān says, in connection with Shuʿayb’s people asking whether his prayer commanded him, that prayer indeed commands and forbids.
TAB-FULL:v18p408/r9.anchor: قال سفيان، " {قالوا يا شعيب أصلاتك تأمرك} [هود: 87] قال: فقال سفيان: إي والله، تأمره وتنهاه "

TAB-FULL:v18p411/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan transmits the Prophet’s warning that prayer which does not restrain a person from indecency and evil only increases his distance from God.
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «من صلى صلاة لم تنهه عن الفحشاء والمنكر لم يزدد بها من الله إلا بعدا»

TAB-FULL:v18p411/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says prayer that does not restrain a person from evil only increases his distance from God.
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: " الصلاة إذا لم تنهه عن الفحشاء والمنكر، قال: من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر، لم يزدد من الله إلا بعدا "

TAB-FULL:v18p411/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r3.speaker: قتادة والحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r3.claim: Qatada and al-Ḥasan likewise say that prayer which fails to restrain from evil only increases distance from God.
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r3.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن، قالا: «من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر، فإنه لا يزداد من الله بذلك إلا بعدا»

TAB-FULL:v18p411/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī holds that prayer itself restrains from evil, as Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masʿūd say; its worshipper is occupied with it and cut off from wrongdoing.
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر، كما قال ابن عباس وابن مسعود.

TAB-FULL:v18p411/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r5.claim: Prayer restrains the person engaged in it because being occupied with prayer interrupts engagement in wrongdoing; obeying it means observing its prescribed bounds.
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r5.anchor: قيل: تنهى من كان فيها، فتحول بينه وبين إتيان الفواحش، لأن شغله بها يقطعه عن الشغل بالمنكر

TAB-FULL:v18p411/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r6.speaker: ابن عون
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAwn says prayer places one in good and bars evil; الفحشاء is adultery and المنكر is disobedience to God, while an act invalidating prayer means there was no prayer.
TAB-FULL:v18p411/r6.anchor: عن ابن عون، في قول الله " {إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: إذا كنت في صلاة

TAB-FULL:v18p414/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن ربيعة وابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r1.claim: Asked by Ibn Abbas, ʿAbd Allāh b. Rabīʿa first guessed that the phrase meant prayer’s glorification, praise, takbīr, Qurʾān recitation, and similar acts; Ibn Abbas rejects the answer as strange and says it means God’s remembrance when people heed His commands and prohibitions.
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن ربيعة، قال: قال لي ابن عباس: " هل تدري ما قوله {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] ؟ قال: قلت: نعم، قال. فما هو؟

TAB-FULL:v18p414/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r2.claim: In another exchange Ibn Abbas answers “prayer and fasting,” then confirms that God’s remembrance of His servants is greater than their remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r2.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: الصلاة والصوم، قال: ذاك ذكر الله

TAB-FULL:v18p414/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas confirms that God’s remembrance of His servants is greater than their remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: صدق والله صاحبك

TAB-FULL:v18p414/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r4.anchor: عن ابن ربيعة، عن ابن عباس قال: «ذكر الله إياكم أكبر من ذكركم إياه»

TAB-FULL:v18p414/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r5.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reports Ibn Abbas’s gloss that God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: جاء رجل إلى ابن عباس، فقال: حدثني عن قول الله

TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r1.claim: ʿIkrima says God’s remembrance of the servant is better than the servant’s remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: ذكر الله للعبد أفضل من ذكره إياه "

TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r2.speaker: عطية
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r2.claim: ʿAṭiyya links the phrase to “Remember Me and I will remember you” and says God’s remembrance of you is greater.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r2.anchor: عن عطية، " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: هو قوله: {فاذكروني أذكركم} [البقرة: 152]، وذكر الله إياكم أكبر من ذكركم إياه "

TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God’s remembrance for His servants when they remember Him is greater than their remembering Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {ولذكر الله} [العنكبوت: 45] لعباده إذا ذكروه {أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] من ذكركم إياه "

TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says God’s remembrance of His servant is greater than the servant’s remembrance of Him in prayer or elsewhere.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: ذكر الله عبده أكبر من ذكر العبد ربه في الصلاة أو غيرها "

TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him; Salman is reported to agree.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «ذكر الله إياكم إذا ذكرتموه أكبر من ذكركم إياه»

TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r6.speaker: سلمان
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r6.claim: Salman is reported to give the same interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي قرة، عن سلمان، مثله

TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r7.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ calls remembrance of God the best deed, more beloved and exalted than fighting an enemy or giving money.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#2/r7.anchor: قال: سمعت أبا الدرداء، يقول: " أخبركم بخير أعمالكم، وأحبها إلى مليككم، وأرفعها في درجاتكم

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r1.speaker: أبو قرة
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r1.claim: Abū Qurra transmits the interpretation that God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r1.anchor: عن جابر، عن عامر، قال: سألت أبا قرة عن قوله " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] ، قال: ذكر الله إياكم أكبر من ذكركم إياه "

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r2.claim: Mujahid and ʿIkrima say God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، وعكرمة، قالا: «ذكر الله إياكم أكبر من ذكركم إياه»

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas connects the saying to 2:152: God’s remembrance of people is greater than their remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r3.anchor: عن عطية، عن ابن عباس، قال: هو كقوله: " {فاذكروني أذكركم} [البقرة: 152]، فذكر الله إياكم أكبر من ذكركم إياه "

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says God’s remembrance of the servant is greater than the servant’s remembrance of his Lord.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r4.anchor: عن شقيق، عن عبد الله: " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: ذكر الله العبد أكبر من ذكر العبد لربه "

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r5.speaker: شعبة
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r5.claim: Shuʿba glosses the phrase as God’s remembrance of you being greater than your remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r5.anchor: عن شعبة، قال: «ذكر الله لكم أكبر من ذكركم له»

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r6.speaker: سلمان
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r6.claim: Salman says remembrance of God is the best deed and nothing is better than it.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r6.anchor: عن العيزار بن حريث، عن رجل، عن سلمان، أنه سئل: " أي العمل أفضل؟ قال: أما تقرأ القرآن {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] ؟ لا شيء أفضل من ذكر الله "

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r7.speaker: أم الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r7.claim: Umm al-Dardāʾ says prayer, fasting, good deeds, and avoiding evil are all remembrance of God, with glorifying Him best.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r7.anchor: عن أم الدرداء، أنها قالت: " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] فإن صليت فهو من ذكر الله، وإن صمت فهو من ذكر الله

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r8.claim: Qatada says nothing is greater than remembrance of God, citing the command to establish prayer for His remembrance.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: لا شيء أكبر من ذكر الله، قال: أكبر الأشياء كلها، وقرأ {أقم الصلاة لذكري} [طه: 14]

TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r9.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r9.claim: Some authorities say the phrase can carry both interpretations: God’s remembrance of people, and people’s remembrance of God as the greatest act.
TAB-FULL:v18p414#3/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: هو محتمل للوجهين جميعا، يعنون القول الأول الذي ذكرناه والثاني.

TAB-FULL:v18p416/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the phrase has two senses: God’s remembrance is greater than everything else, and His remembrance of you is greater than yours of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: لها وجهان: ذكر الله أكبر مما سواه، وذكر الله إياكم أكبر من ذكركم إياه "

TAB-FULL:v18p416/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also interprets it as remembering God when faced with what He has forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس في: " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: لها وجهان: ذكر الله إياكم أكبر من ذكركم إياه، وذكر الله عند ما حرم

TAB-FULL:v18p416/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r3.claim: Abū Mālik, from al-Suddī, says God’s remembrance of the servant during prayer is greater than the prayer itself.
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r3.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي مالك، في قوله " {ولذكر الله أكبر} [العنكبوت: 45] قال: ذكر الله العبد في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة "

TAB-FULL:v18p416/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r4.speaker: ابن عون
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAwn says the worshipper’s prayer and remembrance of God in it are greater than what prayer restrains him from.
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r4.anchor: عن ابن عون، في قول الله " {إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر} [العنكبوت: 45] والذي أنت فيه من ذكر الله أكبر "

TAB-FULL:v18p416/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the apparent sense that God’s remembrance of you is better than your remembrance of Him.
TAB-FULL:v18p416/r5.anchor: وأشبه هذه الأقوال بما دل عليه ظاهر التنزيل قول من قال: ولذكر الله إياكم أفضل من ذكركم إياه.

TABATABAI:29:44-45/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r3.claim: After recounting the fate of shirk and wrongdoing, the passage resumes with the command to recite revelation as a deterrent, through its proofs, stories, exhortations, warnings, promises, and threats; recitation deters both reader and listener.
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r3.anchor: انتقل من ذلك - مستأنفا للكلام - إلى أمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بتلاوة ما أوحي إليه من الكتاب

TABATABAI:29:44-45/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r4.claim: Prayer’s restraint is a natural tendency of its devotional form, not a complete cause that invariably prevents sin.
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r4.anchor: السياق يشهد أن المراد بهذا النهي ردع طبيعة العمل عن الفحشاء والمنكر بنحو الاقتضاء دون العلية التامة

TABATABAI:29:44-45/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r5.claim: Repeated prayer five times daily, especially in a sound community, trains a person away from major sins and other acts rejected by sound nature through instruction and practice.
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r5.anchor: إذ أتى به العبد وهو يكرره كل يوم خمس مرات ويداوم عليه وخاصة إذا زاول عليه في مجتمع صالح

TABATABAI:29:44-45/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r6.claim: Prayer teaches faith in divine unity, prophethood, and judgment; it trains sincere worship, dependence, seeking guidance, humility before God, praise, glorification, and regard for other righteous people.
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r6.anchor: لقنه أولا بما فيه من الذكر الإيمان بوحدانيته تعالى والرسالة وجزاء يوم الجزاء

TABATABAI:29:44-45/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r7.claim: Prayer also trains bodily and clothing purity, avoidance of impurity in clothing and place, and facing the House of God.
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r7.anchor: مضافا إلى حمله إياه على التطهر من الحدث والخبث في بدنه والطهارة في لباسه

TABATABAI:29:44-45/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r8.claim: Even a short period of prayer performed with some sincerity establishes a lasting disposition to avoid indecency and wrongdoing; no other program of self-training demands more.
TABATABAI:29:44-45/r8.anchor: لو داوم على صلاته مدة يسيرة واستعمل في إقامتها بعض الصدق أثبت ذلك في نفسه ملكة الارتداع

TABATABAI:29:45/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45/r1.claim: The difficulty raised is that many worshippers commit grave sins and are not restrained by prayer.
TABATABAI:29:45/r1.anchor: أنا كثيرا ما نجد من المصلين من لا يبالي ارتكاب الكبائر ولا يرتدع عن المنكرات

TABATABAI:29:45/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:29:45/r2.claim: Some interpret prayer as supplication or a call to God’s command, which restrains people; al-Tabataba’i rejects this as departing from the apparent meaning.
TABATABAI:29:45/r2.anchor: ذكر بعضهم أن الصلاة في الآية بمعنى الدعاء والمراد الدعوة إلى أمر الله

TABATABAI:29:45/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45/r3.speaker: آخرون
TABATABAI:29:45/r3.claim: Others take prayer generically to mean that some kinds or instances of prayer restrain from evil; the author says the context concerns prayer’s inherent effect, not only some instances.
TABATABAI:29:45/r3.anchor: وذكر آخرون أن الصلاة في الآية في معنى النكرة والمعنى أن بعض أنواع الصلاة أو أفرادها

TABATABAI:29:45/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45/r4.speaker: قوم
TABATABAI:29:45/r4.claim: Some say prayer restrains only while the worshipper is occupied in it; the author rejects this as too narrow for prayer’s lasting effect.
TABATABAI:29:45/r4.anchor: وذكر قوم أن المراد نهيها عن الفحشاء والمنكر ما دامت قائمة والمصلي في صلاته

TABATABAI:29:45/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:29:45/r5.claim: Some retain the literal sense but argue that prayer only admonishes without guaranteeing obedience, as with God’s command; the author says this mistakes restraint for necessary compulsion.
TABATABAI:29:45/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن الآية على ظاهرها والصلاة بمنزلة من ينهى ويقول لا تفعل كذا ولا تقترف كذا

TABATABAI:29:45/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:29:45/r6.claim: Some say prayer’s remembrance of God prevents disliked acts and at least reduces a worshipper’s wrongdoing; the author rejects making verbal remembrance alone the intended mechanism.
TABATABAI:29:45/r6.anchor: وعن بعضهم في دفع الإشكال أن الصلاة تقام لذكر الله

TABATABAI:29:45/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45/r7.claim: In context, prayer as worship creates a spiritual quality that tends to restrain the soul from indecency and sin; it does not merely describe a subset, the time spent praying, hearing a rebuke, or verbal remembrance alone.
TABATABAI:29:45/r7.anchor: فالمراد به التوسل إلى ملكة الارتداع التي هي من آثار طبيعة الصلاة بنحو الاقتضاء

TABATABAI:29:45#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r1.claim: Prayer is a devotional orientation toward God whose restraining effect is dispositional, not inevitable; obstacles that weaken remembrance, presence, humility, and sincerity weaken that effect.
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r1.anchor: فالحق في الجواب أن الردع أثر طبيعة الصلاة التي هي توجه خاص عبادي إلى الله سبحانه وهو بنحو الاقتضاء دون الاستيجاب

TABATABAI:29:45#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r2.claim: He illustrates the effect comparatively: people who abandon prayer often neglect other duties and lawful distinctions, while even minimal prayer restrains from many acts; greater care in prayer brings greater restraint.
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r2.anchor: وجدته مرتدعا عن كثير مما يقترفه تارك الصلاة غير مكترث به ثم إذا قست إليه من هو فوقه

TABATABAI:29:45#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r3.claim: Al-Raghib defines remembrance first as a mental disposition for retaining acquired knowledge, distinguished from preservation by its emphasis on bringing knowledge to mind; he also uses it for presence in heart or speech.
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r3.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الذكر تارة يقال ويراد به هيئة للنفس بها يمكن للإنسان أن يحفظ ما يقتنيه من المعرفة

TABATABAI:29:45#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r4.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes remembrance after forgetfulness from remembrance sustained without prior forgetting, and says any utterance can be called remembrance.
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r4.anchor: ولذلك قيل الذكر ذكران ذكر عن نسيان وذكر لا عن نسيان بل عن إدامة الحفظ

TABATABAI:29:45#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r5.claim: The author takes the original meaning to be inward remembrance; speech is named remembrance because it contains the inward meaning, with inward remembrance as the effect and intended end of verbal remembrance.
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن الأصل في معناه هو المعنى الأول وتسمية اللفظ ذكرا إنما هو لاشتماله على المعنى القلبي

TABATABAI:29:45#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r6.claim: Prayer is called remembrance because it includes verbal declarations of God’s unity, praise, and transcendence, and because its total form embodies the servant’s worship of God.
TABATABAI:29:45#2/r6.anchor: والصلاة تسمى ذكرا لاشتمالها على الأذكار القولية من تهليل وتحميد وتنزيه

TABATABAI:29:45#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r1.claim: Prayer produces remembrance as its end, as in the command to establish prayer for God’s remembrance; the intended remembrance is inward awareness, restored after absence or sustained continuously.
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r1.anchor: والذكر الذي هو غاية مترتبة على الصلاة أعني الذكر القلبي بمعنى استحضار المذكور

TABATABAI:29:45#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r2.claim: Inward remembrance is the highest human work, the ultimate happiness prepared for humanity, and the key to every good.
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r2.anchor: أفضل عمل يتصور صدوره عن الإنسان وأعلاه كعبا وأعظمه قدرا وأثرا فإنه السعادة الأخيرة

TABATABAI:29:45#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r3.claim: In context, the phrase advances from prayer’s restraint of evil to its greater benefit: inward remembrance, prayer’s end, exceeds the partial good of restraint.
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r3.anchor: ويكون المراد الذكر القلبي الذي يترتب على الصلاة ترتب الغاية على ذي الغاية

TABATABAI:29:45#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r4.claim: Two alternatives are that remembrance means the verbal remembrance contained in prayer or prayer itself as remembrance; either is greater than prayer’s restraining effect.
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r4.anchor: ومن المحتمل أن يراد بالذكر ما تشتمل عليه الصلاة من الذكر أو نفس الصلاة

TABATABAI:29:45#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r5.claim: On both alternatives, remembrance is a genitive construction with the object as its complement, and the comparison is with restraint from indecency and wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:29:45#3/r5.anchor: على الاحتمالين جميعا من المصدر المضاف إلى مفعوله والمفضل عليه

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r1.claim: The cited 2:152 supports the preceding reading that God remembers whoever remembers Him; the source then lists further interpretations of the phrase.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r1.anchor: البقرة 152، وقيل المعنى ذكر الله تعالى العبد أكبر من الصلاة

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r2.claim: Another interpretation says God’s remembrance of the servant is greater than prayer.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r2.anchor: وقيل المعنى ذكر الله تعالى العبد أكبر من الصلاة

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r3.claim: Another interpretation says God’s remembrance of the servant is greater than everything.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r3.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر الله العبد أكبر من كل شيء

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r4.claim: Another view takes the servant’s remembrance of God in prayer to be greater than the other pillars of prayer.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r4.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر العبد لله في الصلاة أكبر من سائر أركان الصلاة

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r5.claim: Another view says a servant’s remembrance of God in prayer is greater than remembrance outside prayer.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r5.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر العبد لله في الصلاة أكبر من ذكره خارج الصلاة

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r6.claim: Another view says a servant’s remembrance of God is greater than the servant’s other deeds.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r6.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر العبد لله أكبر من سائر أعماله

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r7.claim: Another view interprets the phrase to mean that prayer is greater than the other acts of obedience.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r7.anchor: وقيل المعنى للصلاة أكبر من سائر الطاعات

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r8.claim: Another view says remembering God’s prohibition when facing indecency or wrongdoing is a stronger deterrent than prayer’s restraint.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r8.anchor: وقيل المعنى لذكر العبد لله عند الفحشاء والمنكر وذكر نهيه عنهما أكبر من زجر الصلاة

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r9.claim: A further view treats greater as non-comparative and needing no object, by analogy with the statement that what is with God is better than diversion.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r9.anchor: معرى من معنى التفضيل لا يحتاج إلى مفضل عليه كقوله

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r10.claim: The author leaves these interpretations unexamined for brevity, while observing that the arbitrary character of some is apparent.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r10.anchor: فهذه أقوال لهم متفرقة أغمضنا عن البحث عما فيها إيثارا للاختصار

TABATABAI:29:45-46/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r11.claim: God knows good and bad deeds; the verse urges watchfulness, especially under the first interpretation of remembrance.
TABATABAI:29:45-46/r11.anchor: أي ما تفعلونه من خير أو شر فعليكم أن تراقبوه ولا تغفلوا عنه

TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r2.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that prayer which does not restrain from evil only increases distance from God; al-Durr al-Manthur also transmits it via Imran ibn Husayn, Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Umar, and al-Qummi gives it as unconnected.
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r2.anchor: روى أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r3.claim: The Prophet is reported to say there is no prayer for one who does not obey it; obeying prayer means refraining from indecency and evil. Al-Durr al-Manthur also transmits this from Ibn Masud and others.
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r3.anchor: وفيه وأيضا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r4.claim: Anas reports that when told of a young Anṣārī who prayed with the Prophet yet committed immoral acts, the Prophet said his prayer would restrain him someday.
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r4.anchor: وروى أنس أن فتى من الأنصار كان يصلي الصلوات مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r5.claim: Abu Abd Allah says one can judge whether prayer was accepted by seeing whether it restrained its worshipper from evil; acceptance is proportional to that restraint.
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r5.anchor: روى أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من أحب أن يعلم قبلت صلاته

TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Jarud transmits from Abu Ja'far that God’s remembrance of people who pray is greater than their remembrance of Him, as in the promise that God will remember those who remember Him; the author notes this is one previously listed interpretation.
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r6.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r7.claim: A report cited through Majma al-Bayan from Abu Abd Allah defines remembrance as remembering God in relation to what He permits and forbids.
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r7.anchor: عن مجمع البيان وروى أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال ذكر الله عند ما أحل وحرم

TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r8.claim: When Muadh ibn Jabal asked which deeds God loves most, the Prophet answered that one should die with the tongue moist from remembrance of God.
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r8.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أي الأعمال أحب إلى الله

TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r9.claim: The Prophet says the foremost are those who stay awake remembering God, and urges anyone wishing to graze in Paradise’s gardens to remember God often.
TABATABAI:29:41-55#2/r9.anchor: وفيه وقال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABRISI:29:44-45/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:44-45/r6.claim: The Prophet is to recite the Qur’an to those accountable and act according to its contents.
TABRISI:29:44-45/r6.anchor: يعني القرآن أي اقرأه على المكلفين واعمل بما تضمنه

TABRISI:29:44-45/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:44-45/r7.claim: Establish prayer by observing its prescribed limits and times.

TABRISI:29:44-45/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:44-45/r8.claim: Prayer is a divine kindness that helps a responsible person leave rationally and legally reprehensible sins; success is God's enabling, while failure is the person's own fault.
TABRISI:29:44-45/r8.anchor: في هذا دلالة على أن فعل الصلاة لطف للمكلف في ترك القبيح والمعاصي

TABRISI:29:44-45/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:29:44-45/r9.claim: Prayer is like a verbal prohibition: its acts of remembrance, recitation, and standing before God invite their like and repel opposites.
TABRISI:29:44-45/r9.anchor: وقيل: إن الصلاة بمنزلة الناهي بالقول إذا قال: لا تفعل الفحشاء والمنكر

TABRISI:29:44-45/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:29:44-45/r10.claim: Another explanation is that prayer restrains its performer only while the performer is engaged in it.
TABRISI:29:44-45/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن الصلاة تنهى صاحبها عن الفحشاء والمنكر ما دام فيها

TABRISI:29:44-45/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:29:44-45/r11.claim: Prayer ought to restrain its performer, as the verse about entering the Sanctuary says that whoever enters it is safe.
TABRISI:29:44-45/r11.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه ينبغي أن تنهاه كقوله ومن دخله كان آمنا

TABRISI:29:44-45/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:29:44-45/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says prayer contains a restraint from disobeying God; prayer that fails to restrain its performer only increases his distance from God.
TABRISI:29:44-45/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: في الصلاة منهى ومزدجر عن معاصي الله فمن لم تنهه صلاته

TABRISI:29:44-45/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r13.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TABRISI:29:44-45/r13.claim: Hasan and Qatada say prayer that does not restrain its performer from indecency is not truly prayer and becomes a burden against him.
TABRISI:29:44-45/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر فليست صلاته بصلاة

TABRISI:29:44-45/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:44-45/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:29:44-45/r14.claim: Anas al-Juhani transmits the Prophet's saying that one whose prayer does not restrain him from indecency only grows farther from God.
TABRISI:29:44-45/r14.anchor: وروى أنس بن مالك الجهني عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

TABRISI:29:45/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:29:45/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says there is no prayer for one who does not obey prayer, and obeying prayer means leaving indecency and wrongdoing.
TABRISI:29:45/r1.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود أيضا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TABRISI:29:45/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:45/r2.claim: If someone persists in sin after praying, his prayer has not yet matched God's description; repentance later shows that it did benefit and restrain him, even if belatedly.
TABRISI:29:45/r2.anchor: ومعنى ذلك أن الصلاة إذا كانت ناهية عن المعاصي فمن أقامها ثم لم ينته

TABRISI:29:45/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:29:45/r3.claim: Anas relates that, when told a young Ansari prayed with the Prophet but committed indecencies, the Prophet said his prayer would restrain him one day.
TABRISI:29:45/r3.anchor: وروى أنس أن فتى من الأنصار كان يصلي الصلاة مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:29:45/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:29:45/r4.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet said the prayer of a man who prayed by day but stole by night would restrain him.
TABRISI:29:45/r4.anchor: قيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن فلانا يصلي بالنهار

TABRISI:29:45/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:29:45/r5.claim: A report from Abu Abd Allah advises judging prayer's acceptance by whether and how much it prevents indecency and wrongdoing.
TABRISI:29:45/r5.anchor: وروى أصحابنا عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: من أحب أن يعلم أقبلت صلاته

TABRISI:29:45/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وسلمان وابن مسعود ومجاهد
TABRISI:29:45/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, Salman, Ibn Masud, and Mujahid say God's remembrance of people through mercy is greater than their remembrance of Him through obedience.
TABRISI:29:45/r6.anchor: أي ولذكر الله إياكم برحمته أكبر من ذكركم إياه بطاعته عن ابن عباس وسلمان

TABRISI:29:45/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r7.speaker: سلمان وابن زيد وقتادة وأبو الدرداء
TABRISI:29:45/r7.claim: Another view says a servant's remembrance of God exceeds all else and all deeds.
TABRISI:29:45/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه ذكر العبد لربه أكبر مما سواه وأفضل من جميع أعماله عن سلمان

TABRISI:29:45/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:45/r8.claim: On that reading, remembering God's commands, prohibitions, reward, and punishment is the strongest aid to obedience and avoidance of sin.
TABRISI:29:45/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا فيكون تأويله إن أكبر شيء في النهي عن الفحشاء ذكر العبد ربه وأوامره ونواهيه

TABRISI:29:45/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r9.speaker: أبو مالك
TABRISI:29:45/r9.claim: Abu Malik interprets the phrase as God remembering the servant during prayer, greater than the prayer itself.
TABRISI:29:45/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه ذكر الله العبد في الصلاة أكبر من الصلاة عن أبي مالك

TABRISI:29:45/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:29:45/r10.claim: Al-Farraʾ associates remembrance with glorification, sanctification, and declaring God's oneness, which should restrain the worshipper from indecency.
TABRISI:29:45/r10.anchor: عن الفراء أي من كان ذاكرا لله فيجب أن ينهاه ذكره عن الفحشاء والمنكر

TABRISI:29:45/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r11.speaker: ثابت البناني
TABRISI:29:45/r11.claim: Thabit al-Bunani recounts a comparison between freeing four slaves and reciting formulas of remembrance; Habib al-Sulami and his companions knew nothing better than remembrance.
TABRISI:29:45/r11.anchor: وروي عن ثابت البناني: قال إن رجلا أعتق أربع رقاب فقال رجل آخر:

TABRISI:29:45/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r12.speaker: حبيب بن أوفى السلمي وأصحابه
TABRISI:29:45/r12.claim: When asked to compare freeing four slaves with remembrance, Habib al-Sulami and his companions said they knew nothing better than remembrance.
TABRISI:29:45/r12.anchor: فأتى حبيب بن أوفى السلمي وأصحابه فقال: ما تقولون في رجل أعتق أربع رقاب

TABRISI:29:45/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45/r13.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
TABRISI:29:45/r13.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal says no human deed saves more from punishment than remembrance, not even jihad, citing this verse.
TABRISI:29:45/r13.anchor: وعن معاذ بن جبل قال: ما من عمل آدمي عمل أنجى له من عذاب الله

TABRISI:29:45#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:29:45#2/r1.claim: Asked which deeds God loves most, the Prophet answered that one should die with a tongue moist from remembrance; Muadh transmits the exchange.
TABRISI:29:45#2/r1.anchor: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي الأعمال أحب إلى الله قال:

TABRISI:29:45#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:29:45#2/r2.claim: The Prophet calls those who spend nights remembering God the forerunners and urges anyone seeking Paradise's gardens to remember God often.
TABRISI:29:45#2/r2.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " يا معاذ إن السابقين الذين يسهرون بذكر الله عز وجل

TABRISI:29:45#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن ربيعة
TABRISI:29:45#2/r3.claim: Abd Allah ibn Rabiʿa proposes that the best remembrance is recalling God at the moment of sin and restraining oneself.
TABRISI:29:45#2/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن ربيعة قال: قال ابن عباس أرأيت قول الله عز وجل ولذكر الله أكبر قال: قلت

TABRISI:29:45#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:45#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:29:45#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the suggestion remarkable but rejects it, reiterating that God's remembrance of people is greater than their remembrance of Him.
